edges.description: Persistent intracellular and deep-tissue organisms drive the chronic suppurative granulomatous response that forms sulfur granules.
Chronic suppurative granulomatous inflammation coalesces into abscesses and fistulizing lesions.
The chronic inflammatory response produces systemic fever.
Chronic infection produces constitutional weight loss.
Suppurative inflammation of gastrointestinal-site actinomycosis produces abdominal pain.
Abscesses and fistulas extend across normal anatomic barriers rather than respecting them.
Suppurative lesions present clinically as abscesses.
Contiguous suppuration drains through sinus tracts.
In the CNS form, abscess formation presents as brain abscess.
Contiguous infiltration forms an indurated mass that clinically and radiologically resembles a tumor.
Chronic infiltration provokes reactive fibrosis in involved tissue.
Contiguous spread into adjacent bone produces osteomyelitis.
Thoracic contiguous spread to the pleura produces pleural involvement and effusion.
The infiltrative mass presents as a palpable abdominal mass in gastrointestinal-site disease.
A pulmonary mass-forming lesion produces cough.
Pulmonary mass and consolidation produce dyspnea.
Airway and parenchymal involvement produces hemoptysis.
A long-standing IUD provides a chronic nidus and a mucosal breach that lets commensal genital-tract Actinomyces colonize and invade pelvic tissue.
edges.target: Mucosal Barrier Breach and Endogenous Inoculation
